paragraphs.text: Meeting COL-10-01 occurred at Colima on 2010-09-23. A bar owner in contact with the reporting office described a gathering of local businessmen at a restaurant in Colima that the owner initially believed to be a meeting of the port network's financial figures. On further questioning the owner acknowledged that the gathering was a chamber of commerce dinner attended by a state official and that nothing about it suggested criminal activity beyond the presence of two men the owner had seen at the harbor. The reporting office includes the account as background on how the network's figures move in the city's business circles.

The owner described Colima during the period as calm, with the violence that had affected other states largely absent and the business community openly skeptical that a trafficking network operated through the port at all. The owner stated that the men from the harbor are known in the city as shipping agents and are received as such. The owner had no information on any specific load or payment and did not hear the name of any organization.

The reporting office assesses this as low-value background on the social environment in which the network operates. The source has no direct access to the network's decision making and reports on what is visible in public venues. The reporting office cannot exclude that the dinner was used to settle business between the network and the official present, but has no evidence that it was. The account is retained for comparison with later reporting on the same venue.
